contexts.text: Satyrs (). Explained. (This is rendered daemones sylvestres - forest demons in AR 458:2.; and it is said that they) - concupiscences such as those of priapi and satyrs.
(A company of dragonists who appeared afar like satyrs and priapuses. Their cruel sports described.) TCR 388.
It was the appearances of the cupidities with them which were seen as satyrs and priapuses...
The maidens (of Heaven) flee away from such, and tell their companions that they have seen satyrs or priapuses...
I saw a crowd of satyrs in a thick forest. (Their appearance, doings, and conversation, described.)
The satyrs with feet like calves, said, concerning marriages... Those with feet like panthers, said, concerning nature... Those with feet like wolves said, concerning religion...

On seeing me... they began to speak modestly... by which I knew that they were not from the common people. I then told them that I had seen them as satyrs: twenty as calf satyrs; six as panther satyrs; and four as wolf satyrs; at which they wondered, because they had seen themselves as men; in like manner as they saw themselves when with me. I instructed them that they had so appeared from afar from scortatory lust; and that this satyric form is the form of dissolute adultery... They said that they came from Italy, Poland, Germany, England, Sweden; but had never seen anyone from Holland among them.
Adulterers may be compared to... the satyrs and priapuses of the ancients... Moreover, adulterers (there) actually appear as satyrs and priapuses.
How many of the human race are there who have not been born satyrs and priapuses...
On priapuses and satyrs. - Those who have continually thought about adulteries... when seen by the Angels, appear as satyrs. Described.
Forest demons, or satyrs, = cupidities merely corporeal.
Satyrs () = adulterated goods; to dance = joy from a filthy love which has adulterated the good of love. AE 1037:end.
